cards.hint: Recall which letters pair across the ladder rungs.
options: A with T and C with G
A with C and T with G
A with G and T with C
cards.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.
cards.stem: Which base pairing builds the units called base pairs?

cards.hint: Think of the four letters that spell the code.
cards.quote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).
cards.stem: Which set includes the four chemical bases in DNA?

cards.hint: Focus on where most of the material is found.
cards.quote: Most DNA is located in the cell nucleus (where it is called nuclear DNA)
cards.stem: What is most hereditary material in the cell nucleus called?

cards.hint: Think about what happens before cells divide.
options: convert the energy from food into a form that cells can use
cards.quote: An important property of DNA is that it can replicate, or make copies of itself.
cards.stem: What important property lets DNA support new cells during division?
